paragraphs.text: Eula Blue , sometimes called "Eu" by her friends, is a shield mage from New Capenna who was invited to join the first official multiplanar class of Strixhaven University on Arcavios . She aspired to join Silverquill , the college of eloquence and debate.
Eula is an attractive light-skinned girl with white-blond hair. She is a self-trained shieldmage , able to project defensive forcefields.

She grew up in the upper Mezzio , where her parents aspired to Park Heights . Etiquette is very important to her, and she always tries to push for social acceptance. Though she often hides her thoughts behind a veneer of polite manners, she is ambitious and willing to put in the hard work to get what she wants, even when doing so is a bit risky. She understands that words are both weapons and shields, and though she doesn't like to rely on others, she is fiercely protective of her friends.

Eula was recruited for Strixhaven by Professor Kasmina , because she had been identified as an ember ; a potential Planeswalker and powerful wizard. It is unknown if the Desparkening had any influence on her potential to ignite . This may yet come true under the right conditions. Unlike her four classmates, Eula doesn't hail from a powerful wizard family.

Eula was supposed to rise through the ranks of one of the Families in New Capenna, learning the art of magic and the cunning of commerce. Although her father wanted her to join the Brokers , she herself wanted to join the Obscura . But that was before the war came — before the fight for the Multiverse devastated her home, and with it her hopes for a magical education. Now, the streets were paved with dust and rubble, and only the clean-up Riveteers crews were hiring.

But the destruction of the war also brought something new: the ability to travel to other planes . Travel to other worlds was once reserved for a special few who could walk between planes . Now, the Multiverse was open to all. This abstract idea became very real for Eula when she received an invitation to study at a magical school built on a different plane of existence . Given a chance to return to her study of magic, Eula leapt to take it. She may never have heard of “ Strixhaven University ,” and she certainly didn’t apply to join its first official multiplanar class. Still, a fully funded trip to a new plane, a new future, was something she couldn’t refuse.

What she didn’t expect was the kinship she felt with her fellow students, like Alandra , a merfolk girl with a flair for art and mischief, and the mysterious boy Segante . The other two students in her class were the gentle minotaur Jamira and the inquisitive Kequia Akosa . Eula shared a bedroom with Alandra and bonded with Segante by doing his laundry for a fee.

Because her father had been loath to let her go, he had expected her to provide him with information that would allow him to move up in the Brokers' ranks. For this reason, Eula early on started copying spells from the Biblioplex and sending the copies home through the Omenpaths mail system.

But Strixhaven, too, was a victim of the war, and the arrival of Eula and her friends pressed on its wounds. Not everyone was thrilled by the school’s new students, and their presence was a constant reminder of how the Multiverse was forever changed. Eula and the other multiplanar students quickly became a target for enemies within and without. Although they bonded, they found that various forces were active to isolate them emotionally from each other. In a secret plot, Professor Kasmina endeavored to create tensions between the classmates.

During one a confrontation with anonymous bullies at Sedgemoor , Eula discovered that she could use black mana as well as white to create her shields. Later, the Arcavios Preservation Society abducted her and tried to maker disappear in a collapsing Omenpath. She was saved by Segante, which led to them starting an intimate relationship.

It was revealed that Kasmina had selected the five students because they had the potential to be powerful planeswalkers. Her underlying purpose was to force them to ignite under stressful circumstances, and to rob their sparks to reignite her own. This plot was thwarted by the five students combining their powers, and Kasmina presumably died in the final confrontation in the heart of a snarl .

Afterward, Professor Vess had to task to to punish the five students for their various transgressions, with consideration of Kasmina's role. She allowed them to stay on and pledge to their individual colleges, but forbade them to relocate to the appropriate dorms. This also allowed them to serve as residential advisors to the next incoming class of cross-planar students.
